## Findings

### 1. **tree-sitter-cli cargo fallback libclang error**
**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml`

The tree-sitter npm task reports `ok` instead of failing because it has `failed_when: false` (line 317), masking timeouts and errors. The cargo fallback chain is:
- Line 309: `treesitter_check.rc != 0` — computed from line 274-283 as an aggregate
- Lines 274-283: `treesitter_check` is `rc: 1` if **either** `treesitter_version_check.rc != 0` (no tree-sitter anywhere) **OR** `treesitter_mise_cleanup.changed` (just purged broken mise npm binary)
- Line 272: Cleanup marks changed only if "BROKEN" appears in stdout (missing/non-executable native binary in mise node_modules)
- Line 332: Cargo task depends on `treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0`

**Problem:** On CentOS 7, the "Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm" task at line 293 doesn't run at all because on old glibc systems (detected in config.toml.tmpl lines 8-19), `node` is **not** in the `[tools]` section — it's explicitly skipped. So `mise exec -- npm` falls back to system npm (v8.19.4), which installs to system `/usr/lib/node_modules` requiring sudo. The npm task reports `ok` (not executed or succeeded quietly with no "added" marker), setting `treesitter_npm` undefined, and the cargo fallback at line 363 then fails with libclang errors because clang-devel wasn't installed on RedHat.

### 2. **coding_agents npm EACCES failures (Copilot, Codex, Gemini, OpenChamber)**
**Files:**
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` lines 156-172 (Copilot), 223-239 (Codex), 286-302 (Gemini), 1152-1168 (OpenChamber)
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` lines 30-59

All four tasks use `mise exec -- npm install -g <pkg>` to install globally, but on CentOS 7, **node is not in mise's `[tools]`** (config.toml detects oldEL=true and skips node entirely, lines 30-43). This causes `mise exec` to find no managed node, falling back to system node (v16.20.2, npm 8.19.4), which tries to write to `/usr/lib/node_modules` without sudo → EACCES permission denied.

**Root cause:** Lines 30-43 in config.toml.tmpl skip `node = "lts"` entirely on CentOS 7, documented as a baseline compatibility decision (line 33 comment says Node.js requires separate manual install via NodeSource RPM).

### 3. **rust_cargo_tools Rust 1.95.0 mirror 404**
**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml` line 19

The task runs `mise install rust@latest`, which downloads from the mirror specified in `~/.cargo/config.toml` (configured elsewhere to use `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup`). The tuna mirror doesn't carry 1.95.0 (too new or garbage-collected). 

**Solution options:**
- Pin a known-available version (e.g., `rust@1.84` or similar) instead of `@latest`
- Set `RUSTUP_INIT_SKIP_PATH_CHECK=yes` and use official mirror as fallback via env var (if mise's rustup respects it)
- Fall back to official rustup if tuna fails

The task has no fallback logic; it silently succeeds/fails without detecting mirror unavailability.

**Issue 1 (tree-sitter libclang):** The task "Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm" (line 293) skips on CentOS 7 because `node` is not in mise's `[tools]` (config.toml.tmpl:30-43 detects oldEL=true and omits it). Without mise-managed node, `mise exec -- npm` falls back to system npm (8.19.4), writing to `/usr/lib/node_modules`. When that fails with EACCES, the cargo fallback at line 363 runs but fails with libclang errors because the preceding RedHat clang-devel install (line 342) depends on `treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0` — and since npm didn't actually run (skipped by condition), `treesitter_npm` is undefined, defaulting to 1, causing clang-devel to install but the cargo build still lacks libclang headers.

**Issue 2 (coding_agents npm EACCES):** All four agents (Copilot line 156, Codex line 223, Gemini line 286, OpenChamber line 1152) run `mise exec -- npm install -g <pkg>`. On CentOS 7, mise has no node, so npm falls back to system npm (8.19.4), trying to write to `/usr/lib/node_modules` → EACCES. The tasks don't guard against this; they run unconditionally on Debian/RedHat.

**Issue 3 (rust 1.95.0 404):** Line 19 installs `rust@latest` via the TUNA mirror configured in `~/.cargo/config.toml`. TUNA doesn't have 1.95.0. No fallback to official mirror or version pinning.

568	    - codexbar_macos_check.rc != 0
569	  community.general.homebrew_cask:
570	    name: codexbar
571	    state: present
572	
573	- name: Check if CodexBar is installed (Linux)
574	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
575	  ansible.builtin.command: which codexbar
576	  register: codexbar_check
577	  changed_when: false
578	  failed_when: false
579	
580	- name: Check if Homebrew (Linuxbrew) is available
581	  when:
582	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
583	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
584	  ansible.builtin.command: command -v brew
585	  register: codexbar_brew_check
586	  changed_when: false
587	  failed_when: false
588	
589	- name: Install CodexBar via Linuxbrew (preferred)
590	  when:
591	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
592	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
593	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc == 0
594	  block:
595	    - name: Tap steipete/tap for CodexBar (Linuxbrew)
596	      community.general.homebrew_tap:
597	        name: steipete/tap
598	        state: present
599	
600	    - name: Install CodexBar (Linuxbrew)
601	      community.general.homebrew:
602	        name: codexbar
603	        state: present
604	  rescue:
605	    - name: Mark Linuxbrew install as failed
606	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
607	        codexbar_brew_failed: true
608	
609	- name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (CodexBar fallback)
610	  when:
611	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
612	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
613	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc != 0 or (codexbar_brew_failed | default(false))
614	  ansible.builtin.file:
615	    path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
616	    state: directory
617	    mode: '0755'
618	
619	- name: Get latest CodexBar release (Linux fallback)
620	  when:
621	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
622	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
623	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc != 0 or (codexbar_brew_failed | default(false))
624	  ansible.builtin.uri:
625	    url: https://api.github.com/repos/steipete/CodexBar/releases/latest
626	    return_content: true
627	  register: codexbar_release
628	
629	- name: Compute CodexBar arch and tag (Linux fallback)
630	  when:
631	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
632	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
633	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc != 0 or (codexbar_brew_failed | default(false))
634	    - codexbar_release is defined
635	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
636	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
637	    codexbar_arch: "{{ target_architecture }}"
638	    codexbar_tag: "{{ codexbar_release.json.tag_name.startswith('v') | ternary(codexbar_release.json.tag_name, 'v' ~ codexbar_release.json.tag_name) }}"
639	
640	- name: Compute CodexBar release asset name (Linux fallback)
641	  when:
642	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
643	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
644	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc != 0 or (codexbar_brew_failed | default(false))
645	    - codexbar_tag is defined
646	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
647	    codexbar_asset: "CodexBarCLI-{{ codexbar_tag }}-linux-{{ codexbar_arch }}.tar.gz"
648	
649	- name: Install CodexBar from GitHub releases (Linux fallback)
650	  when:
651	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
652	    - codexbar_check.rc != 0
653	    - codexbar_brew_check.rc != 0 or (codexbar_brew_failed | default(false))
654	    - codexbar_asset is defined
655	  block:
656	    - name: Download CodexBar release (Linux fallback)
657	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
658	        url: "https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/releases/download/{{ codexbar_tag }}/{{ codexbar_asset }}"
659	        dest: /tmp/codexbar.tar.gz
660	        mode: '0644'
661	        timeout: 120
662	      retries: 3
663	      delay: 5
664	
665	    - name: Create temp directory for CodexBar extraction (Linux fallback)
666	      ansible.builtin.file:
667	        path: /tmp/codexbar
668	        state: directory
669	        mode: '0755'
670	
671	    - name: Extract CodexBar release (Linux fallback)
672	      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
673	        src: /tmp/codexbar.tar.gz
674	        dest: /tmp/codexbar
675	        remote_src: true
676	
677	    - name: Find codexbar binary (Linux fallback)
678	      ansible.builtin.find:
679	        paths: /tmp/codexbar
680	        patterns: CodexBarCLI
681	        file_type: file
682	      register: codexbar_find
683	
684	    - name: Install CodexBar to ~/.local/bin (Linux fallback)
685	      when: codexbar_find.matched | default(0) | int > 0
686	      ansible.builtin.copy:
687	        src: "{{ codexbar_find.files[0].path }}"
688	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/codexbar"
689	        mode: '0755'
690	        remote_src: true
691	
692	    - name: Clean up CodexBar temp files (Linux fallback)
693	      ansible.builtin.file:
694	        path: "{{ item }}"
695	        state: absent
696	      loop:
697	        - /tmp/codexbar.tar.gz
698	        - /tmp/codexbar
699	
700	  rescue:
701	    - name: Warn CodexBar installation failed
702	      ansible.builtin.debug:
703	        msg: "CodexBar installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
704	
705	    - name: Clean up CodexBar temp files after failure
706	      ansible.builtin.file:
707	        path: "{{ item }}"
708	        state: absent
709	      loop:
710	        - /tmp/codexbar.tar.gz
711	        - /tmp/codexbar

909	        - /tmp/td

917	      ansible.builtin.file:
918	        path: "{{ item }}"
919	        state: absent

1098	# === Specify CLI ===
1099	
1100	- name: Check if uv is available
1101	  ansible.builtin.command: which uv
1102	  register: uv_check
1103	  changed_when: false
1104	  failed_when: false
1105	
1106	- name: Check if Specify CLI is installed
1107	  ansible.builtin.command: which specify
1108	  register: specify_check
1109	  changed_when: false
1110	  failed_when: false
1111	
1112	- name: Install Specify CLI via uv
1113	  when:
1114	    - uv_check.rc == 0
1115	    - specify_check.rc != 0
1116	  ansible.builtin.command: uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
1117	  register: specify_install
1118	  until: specify_install is succeeded
1119	  retries: 3
1120	  delay: 5
1121	  args:
1122	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/specify"
1123	  environment:
1124	    GIT_HTTP_VERSION: HTTP/1.1
1125	
1126	- name: Warn when uv is missing and Specify CLI is not installed
1127	  when:
1128	    - uv_check.rc != 0

1145	    - openchamber_check.rc != 0

1149	    state: present

1152	- name: Install OpenChamber via mise npm (Linux, user-level no-sudo)

1155	    - openchamber_check.rc != 0

1159	    elif command -v mise >/dev/null 2>&1; then

1172	# Install-only by design: the helper exits early without any network access when
1173	# a claude-hud cache or installed_plugins.json entry already exists. Explicit
1174	# upgrades are handled by `just upgrade-plugins`.

1176	# Why `ansible_facts.python.executable` instead of literal `python3`?
1177	# claude_hud_sync.py uses `from __future__ import annotations` (Py3.7+
1178	# syntax) plus `@dataclass`. CentOS 7's `/usr/bin/python3` is 3.6.8 which
1179	# can't parse `from __future__ import annotations` and aborts with

1181	# `ansible_facts.python.executable` is the interpreter ansible itself
1182	# discovered/was-told-to-use (which on CentOS 7 is the uv-managed 3.13
1183	# we override via the controlling chezmoi script — see
1184	# .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl).
1185	- name: Install claude-hud plugin on first apply only
1186	  ansible.builtin.command:
1187	    argv:
1188	      - "{{ ansible_facts.python.executable | default('python3') }}"
1189	      - "{{ role_path }}/files/claude_hud_sync.py"
1190	      - --only-if-missing
1191	  register: claude_hud_sync
1192	  changed_when: "'status=changed' in claude_hud_sync.stdout"
1193	  ignore_errors: true

293	- name: Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm (Debian/Ubuntu)
294	  # The npm tarball comes from npmmirror (when useChineseMirror=true), but the
295	  # postinstall script `node install.js` ALWAYS downloads a prebuilt binary
296	  # from `https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter/releases/download/...`
297	  # which redirects to release-assets.githubusercontent.com (Azure blob CDN).
298	  # That CDN is frequently unreachable / extremely slow from China, and
299	  # tree-sitter's install.js has no env-var override for the download URL.
300	  # Without an outer timeout the whole `chezmoi apply` hangs indefinitely.
301	  #
302	  # `timeout 180` exits 124 on timeout → treesitter_npm.rc != 0 → cargo
303	  # fallback fires (cargo crates.io is mirrored via TUNA when
304	  # useChineseMirror=true, so cargo path is reliable behind GFW). 180s is
305	  # enough for a working network (full install ~30s) but bounded enough not
306	  # to burn the fleet-apply outer budget.
307	  when:
308	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
309	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
310	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
311	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
312	    timeout 180 {{ mise_bin }} exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli
313	  args:
314	    executable: /bin/bash
315	  register: treesitter_npm
316	  changed_when: "'added' in treesitter_npm.stdout or 'added' in treesitter_npm.stderr"
317	  failed_when: false  # Don't fail the play; downstream cargo task handles it.
318	
319	# cargo build of tree-sitter-cli requires libclang (via bindgen). Install on
320	# Debian/Ubuntu when we might fall through to the cargo path.
321	#
322	# Why os_family and not ansible_pkg_mgr? On CentOS 7 the ansible-core
323	# 2.18+ pkg_mgr auto-detection fails (no dnf binary), leaving
324	# ansible_pkg_mgr undefined. os_family is always populated.
325	- name: Install libclang-dev for tree-sitter-cli cargo build (Debian/Ubuntu)
326	  # rc != 0 covers both: regular npm failure AND `timeout` exit 124.
327	  # `is failed` alone wouldn't catch rc=124 because failed_when: false above.
328	  when:
329	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
330	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
331	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
332	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
333	  become: true
334	  tags: [sudo]
335	  ansible.builtin.apt:
336	    name: libclang-dev
337	    state: present
338	  ignore_errors: true

340	# RedHat equivalent: `clang-devel` (provides libclang). yum CLI for CentOS 7
341	# compat — see pitfalls/centos7-ansible-yum-dnf-backend.md.
342	- name: Install clang-devel for tree-sitter-cli cargo build (RedHat/CentOS)
343	  when:
344	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "RedHat"
345	    - treesitter_check.rc != 0
346	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
347	    - treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0
348	  become: true
349	  tags: [sudo]
350	  ansible.builtin.shell: |
351	    set -e
352	    if rpm -q clang-devel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
353	      echo "ALL_INSTALLED"
354	      exit 0
355	    fi
356	    yum install -y clang-devel
357	  args:
358	    executable: /bin/bash
359	  register: clang_yum_result
360	  changed_when: "'ALL_INSTALLED' not in clang_yum_result.stdout"
361	  ignore_errors: true

Excellent. Now I have all the information needed. Let me compile the findings.

## Findings

### 1. **tree-sitter-cli cargo fallback libclang error**
**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/lazyvim_deps/tasks/main.yml`

The tree-sitter npm task reports `ok` instead of failing because it has `failed_when: false` (line 317), masking timeouts and errors. The cargo fallback chain is:
- Line 309: `treesitter_check.rc != 0` — computed from line 274-283 as an aggregate
- Lines 274-283: `treesitter_check` is `rc: 1` if **either** `treesitter_version_check.rc != 0` (no tree-sitter anywhere) **OR** `treesitter_mise_cleanup.changed` (just purged broken mise npm binary)
- Line 272: Cleanup marks changed only if "BROKEN" appears in stdout (missing/non-executable native binary in mise node_modules)
- Line 332: Cargo task depends on `treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0`

**Problem:** On CentOS 7, the "Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm" task at line 293 doesn't run at all because on old glibc systems (detected in config.toml.tmpl lines 8-19), `node` is **not** in the `[tools]` section — it's explicitly skipped. So `mise exec -- npm` falls back to system npm (v8.19.4), which installs to system `/usr/lib/node_modules` requiring sudo. The npm task reports `ok` (not executed or succeeded quietly with no "added" marker), setting `treesitter_npm` undefined, and the cargo fallback at line 363 then fails with libclang errors because clang-devel wasn't installed on RedHat.

### 2. **coding_agents npm EACCES failures (Copilot, Codex, Gemini, OpenChamber)**
**Files:**
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/tasks/main.yml` lines 156-172 (Copilot), 223-239 (Codex), 286-302 (Gemini), 1152-1168 (OpenChamber)
- `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` lines 30-59

All four tasks use `mise exec -- npm install -g <pkg>` to install globally, but on CentOS 7, **node is not in mise's `[tools]`** (config.toml detects oldEL=true and skips node entirely, lines 30-43). This causes `mise exec` to find no managed node, falling back to system node (v16.20.2, npm 8.19.4), which tries to write to `/usr/lib/node_modules` without sudo → EACCES permission denied.

**Root cause:** Lines 30-43 in config.toml.tmpl skip `node = "lts"` entirely on CentOS 7, documented as a baseline compatibility decision (line 33 comment says Node.js requires separate manual install via NodeSource RPM).

### 3. **rust_cargo_tools Rust 1.95.0 mirror 404**
**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml` line 19

The task runs `mise install rust@latest`, which downloads from the mirror specified in `~/.cargo/config.toml` (configured elsewhere to use `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup`). The tuna mirror doesn't carry 1.95.0 (too new or garbage-collected). 

**Solution options:**
- Pin a known-available version (e.g., `rust@1.84` or similar) instead of `@latest`
- Set `RUSTUP_INIT_SKIP_PATH_CHECK=yes` and use official mirror as fallback via env var (if mise's rustup respects it)
- Fall back to official rustup if tuna fails

The task has no fallback logic; it silently succeeds/fails without detecting mirror unavailability.

---

## Summary (under 400 words)

**Issue 1 (tree-sitter libclang):** The task "Install tree-sitter-cli via mise npm" (line 293) skips on CentOS 7 because `node` is not in mise's `[tools]` (config.toml.tmpl:30-43 detects oldEL=true and omits it). Without mise-managed node, `mise exec -- npm` falls back to system npm (8.19.4), writing to `/usr/lib/node_modules`. When that fails with EACCES, the cargo fallback at line 363 runs but fails with libclang errors because the preceding RedHat clang-devel install (line 342) depends on `treesitter_npm.rc | default(1) != 0` — and since npm didn't actually run (skipped by condition), `treesitter_npm` is undefined, defaulting to 1, causing clang-devel to install but the cargo build still lacks libclang headers.

**Issue 2 (coding_agents npm EACCES):** All four agents (Copilot line 156, Codex line 223, Gemini line 286, OpenChamber line 1152) run `mise exec -- npm install -g <pkg>`. On CentOS 7, mise has no node, so npm falls back to system npm (8.19.4), trying to write to `/usr/lib/node_modules` → EACCES. The tasks don't guard against this; they run unconditionally on Debian/RedHat.

**Issue 3 (rust 1.95.0 404):** Line 19 installs `rust@latest` via the TUNA mirror configured in `~/.cargo/config.toml`. TUNA doesn't have 1.95.0. No fallback to official mirror or version pinning.

```text
1	# `centos_server` profile on a noRoot CentOS 7 box installs nothing
2	
3	## Symptom
4	
5	Run `chezmoi apply` on a CentOS Linux 7.9 box where the user has no
6	`sudo` (typical corporate/data-center development server):
7	
8	```
9	$ sudo -v
10	sudo: PAM account management error: Permission denied
11	sudo: a password is required
12	```
13	
14	`chezmoi apply` completes cleanly, ansible reports `0 failed`, configs
15	deploy under `~/.config/`, but `command -v rg fd jq nvim starship`
16	returns nothing. The dotfiles-deployed `~/.zshrc` references binaries
17	that don't exist; opening a new shell prints `command not found` for
18	half the prompt.
19	
20	## Root cause
21	
22	The Linux ansible roles have two parallel install paths for each tool:
23	
24	1. **System-level** (`apt:` / `yum:`) — gated by `become: true, tags:
25	   [sudo]`. Skipped on `noRoot=true` via `--skip-tags sudo`. Correct.
26	2. **User-level fallback** — downloads pre-built binaries from GitHub
27	   releases into `~/.local/bin/`, no sudo required.
28	
29	The user-level fallback is the one that's *supposed* to fire on a
30	noRoot box. It was historically gated on
31	`when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` — which made sense when
32	the only Linux profiles were `ubuntu_*`, but is wrong as soon as a
33	RedHat-family box (CentOS, Rocky, Alma) shows up. The user-level path
34	has no apt-specific behaviour — it's `curl | tar | install`. There's
35	no reason for it to be gated on the package-manager family.
36	
37	So on CentOS 7 with `noRoot=true`, both paths are gated out:
38	
39	- system-level: skipped by `--skip-tags sudo`
40	- user-level: skipped by `os_family == "Debian"` predicate
41	
42	The role is a no-op and the user gets a working `~/.zshrc` pointing at
43	binaries that were never installed.
44	
45	## Fix
46	
47	Broaden the user-level (non-sudo-tagged) `when:` predicates from:
48	
49	```yaml
50	when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
51	```
52	
53	to:
54	
55	```yaml
56	when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
57	```
58	
59	Applied across `dot_ansible/roles/{base,starship,security_tools,rust_cargo_tools}/tasks/main.yml`
60	when the `centos_server` profile was introduced. The
61	`Re-check if X is installed` + `Install X from GitHub releases
62	(user-level, no sudo)` block pattern is the canonical shape — every
63	file that has it needs the broadening.
64	
65	**Don't** broaden the sudo-tagged `apt:` blocks the same way — those
66	have `become: true, tags: [sudo]` and use `ansible.builtin.apt:` which
67	fails on RedHat. Either leave them alone (skipped under `--skip-tags
68	sudo` anyway) or add a parallel `RedHat` block with `ansible.builtin.yum:`.
69	
70	## CentOS 7-specific notes (glibc 2.17)
71	
72	CentOS 7 ships glibc 2.17 (released 2012). Many modern GitHub-release
73	binaries are built on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (glibc 2.35+) and crash
74	with:
75	
76	```
77	./tool: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.29' not found (required by ./tool)
78	```
79	
80	### CentOS 7 also ships Python 3.6.8 — bootstrap pins ansible to Python 3.13
81	
82	Symptom on a fresh CentOS 7 box:
83	
84	```
85	[INFO] Installing ansible via uv...
86	Resolved 10 packages in 4m 29s
87	Installed 10 packages …
88	 + ansible-core==2.11.12          ← suspicious: latest is 2.18+
89	…
90	[INFO] Installing ansible-galaxy collections...
91	[WARNING]: Skipping Galaxy server https://galaxy.ansible.com/api/. Got an
92	unexpected error when getting available versions of collection community.general:
93	'/api/v3/plugin/ansible/content/published/collections/index/community/general/versions/'
94	ERROR! Unexpected Exception, this is probably a bug:
95	'/api/v3/plugin/ansible/content/published/collections/index/community/general/versions/'
96	[ERROR] Failed to install community.general collection.
97	chezmoi: 00_bootstrap.sh: exit status 1
98	```
99	
100	Two compounding issues:
101	
102	1. **`uv tool install` defaults to system Python.** On CentOS 7 that's
103	   Python 3.6.8. uv resolves `ansible-core` to **2.11.12** — the last
104	   version with Py3.6 support, released August 2021.
105	2. **2.11.12 predates Galaxy NG.** `galaxy.ansible.com` was migrated to
106	   the Pulp/Galaxy-NG backend; ansible-core 2.11 hits the new
107	   `/api/v3/plugin/ansible/content/published/...` endpoint and throws
108	   `KeyError(<that URL string>)` because it expects the legacy v2
109	   shape. Output makes it look like a network/proxy error — it's not.
110	   The proxy hint in the bootstrap script's error message is a red
111	   herring on CentOS 7.
112	
113	**Fix (already in `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl`):** install
114	ansible with `uv tool install --force --python 3.13 ansible-core`. uv
115	auto-fetches a python-build-standalone interpreter (statically linked,
116	glibc-2.17 compatible) and pulls modern ansible-core (2.18+) that
117	speaks Galaxy NG. Same pattern as `pre-commit` in
118	`dot_ansible/roles/security_tools/tasks/main.yml`.
119	
120	The bootstrap also detects an existing ansible install on Python <3.10
121	and force-reinstalls — so a box that previously bootstrapped with the
122	old line auto-heals on the next `chezmoi apply`. If you want to nuke
123	manually: `uv tool uninstall ansible-core && rm -rf
124	~/.local/share/uv/tools/ansible-core`.
125	
126	
127	
128	The user-level fallbacks in `base/tasks/main.yml` already prefer
129	**musl** assets where upstream offers them — `ripgrep`, `fd`, `lnav`
130	all ship `*-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` variants that are statically
131	linked and ignore glibc version. Those are fine on CentOS 7.
132	
133	Tools that ship glibc-only binaries (some Go releases, some Rust
134	releases without musl variants) will fail. Workarounds, in order of
135	preference:
136	
137	1. **Cargo source build** — `cargo install <crate>` works on CentOS 7
138	   via the user's mise/cargo toolchain (`rust_cargo_tools` role
139	   already sets this up).
140	2. **Older release pin** — find a release built before the upstream
141	   project moved to a newer Ubuntu CI, pin to it.
142	3. **Skip on CentOS 7** — for tools that aren't critical, gate the
143	   block on `ansible_distribution_major_version != "7"` and live
144	   without it.
145	
146	If the box gets rebuilt as Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 (glibc 2.28 / 2.34), most
147	of these go away — the gate-broadening fix above is still correct on
148	those.
149	
150	## Required preconditions on a noRoot CentOS box
151	
152	The dotfiles can't install **everything** without sudo. On
153	`centos_server` + `noRoot=true`, verify before running `chezmoi apply`:
154	
155	- `command -v zsh` resolves — `zsh` package install needs sudo. Most
156	  corporate CentOS 7 boxes ship zsh; if not, ask the admin to
157	  `yum install zsh`.
158	- `command -v git` resolves — same story.
159	- `chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)"` — depends on the box's chsh policy
160	  (usually no sudo needed but `/etc/shells` must list zsh's path).
161	
162	## Migration note
163	
164	If/when this CentOS 7 box gets rebuilt as Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 (or any
165	modern RedHat-family distro), the gate-broadening change in this fix
166	remains correct (`os_family == "RedHat"` still matches). The
167	glibc-2.17 caveat goes away. The `yum:` blocks added to `base`,
168	`zsh`, `ruby_gem_tools` continue to work — `yum:` is an alias for
169	`dnf:` on RHEL 8+ via the ansible compatibility shim.
170	
171	## How to repro locally (Docker)
172	
173	Two `docker-compose` images mirror the corporate CentOS 7 box and a
174	modern Rocky 9 sister target:
175	
176	```bash
177	# Closest reproduction of the actual box (CentOS 7 + noRoot=true)
178	just docker-run-centos7-noroot
179	# Inside container, the user-level fallbacks should have populated
180	# ~/.local/bin: command -v rg fd jq starship zsh just bats
181	
182	# Modern dnf-native sister case (Rocky Linux 9, glibc 2.34)
183	just docker-run-rocky9-noroot
184	
185	# Bats smoke suite under both
186	just docker-test-centos-all
187	```
188	
189	The CentOS 7 Dockerfile (`Dockerfile.centos7`) redirects
190	`/etc/yum.repos.d/CentOS-*.repo` to `vault.centos.org` since CentOS 7
191	EOL'd 2024-06-30 and the default `mirrorlist.centos.org` returns 404.
192	The user's actual corporate box may still be on an internal mirror;
193	the vault redirect only matters for the Docker reproduction.
194	
195	Use the sudo flavor (`just docker-run-centos7`) when you need to
196	exercise the `yum:` task branches in `base`/`zsh`/`ruby_gem_tools` —
197	just be aware that Debian-only roles (`devtools`, `lazyvim_deps`,
198	`docker`, etc.) still lack yum branches and will fail; those services
199	are configured with `allowPartialFailure=true` so the apply finishes
200	and you get a complete failure list.
201	
202	## Related
203	
204	- `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml` — canonical
205	  `Re-check if X / Install X from GitHub releases (user-level)`
206	  pattern.
207	- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
208	  — `centos_server` profile branch + `--skip-tags sudo` on
209	  `noRoot=true`.
210	- `Dockerfile.centos7` / `Dockerfile.rocky9` + `docker-compose.yml`
211	  `centos7*` / `rocky9*` services — local install-test infrastructure.
212	- `pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md` — sibling pitfall: the
213	  inverse of this one (sudo task without the `[sudo]` tag, fails on
214	  noRoot).
215
```

All three failures share the same root cause: on CentOS 7, `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` (lines 30-43) intentionally omits `node` and `rust` from mise's `[tools]` because of glibc 2.17 / TUNA-mirror gaps — but the ansible roles don't know that and blindly call `mise exec -- npm …` (falls back to system node 16 → EACCES on `/usr/lib`) or `mise install rust@latest` (hits TUNA mirror missing 1.95.0).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-09 12:07:46Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**On CentOS 7, the npm-based CLIs (Copilot/Codex/Gemini/OpenChamber/tree-sitter-cli) can't be installed via mise (no managed node) and won't work with system node v16 (most require node ≥18/20). How do you want to handle them?**

Options:
- **Skip cleanly on EL7 (Recommended)** - Detect mise-managed node; if absent, log a one-line skip and move on. No EACCES, no half-broken installs. Document manual NodeSource RPM install in pitfalls.
- **Install Node ≥20 via NodeSource as a sudo task** - Add a yum-based NodeSource setup (needs sudo) so mise-or-system node ≥20 is present, then run the npm tasks. More work, more sudo surface.
- **Use system node 16 with user prefix** - Run `npm install -g --prefix ~/.local …` to bypass /usr/lib EACCES. Will install but most packages will warn/fail at runtime due to node <20.

**On CentOS 7, `mise install rust@latest` hits TUNA mirror gap (no 1.95.0). Fix?**

Options:
- **Skip mise rust on EL7, use rustup-init directly (Recommended)** - Gate `mise install rust@latest` on `not oldEL`. On EL7 use `curl https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable` (the workaround the mise config.toml.tmpl already documents in its comment block).
- **Override RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER for the mise install** - Pass `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER=https://static.rust-lang.org` in the task env so mise's rustup ignores TUNA. Smaller change but still goes through mise.
- **Pin a specific rust version known to be on TUNA** - Replace `rust@latest` with e.g. `rust@1.84.0`. Brittle — needs occasional bumping when TUNA GCs old versions.


**Answer:** Skip cleanly on EL7 (Recommended), Skip mise rust on EL7, use rustup-init directly (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

```md
# CentOS 7 (`idc-server104`) chezmoi-apply failures — fix plan

## Context

User `yczhang` ran `chezmoi update --apply --init` on a CentOS 7.9 box (`centos_server` profile, passwordless sudo) and hit five ansible task failures:

| # | Task | Error | Root cause |
|---|------|-------|------------|
| 1 | `lazyvim_deps : Install tree-sitter-cli via cargo (fallback)` | `Unable to find libclang … libclangAST.so.7 cannot open` | Cargo path triggered because the prior `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` couldn't actually use mise's node (none managed on EL7); CentOS 7's `clang-devel` is split and the cargo+bindgen build fails to link libclang at runtime. |
| 2 | `coding_agents : Install GitHub Copilot CLI via mise npm` | `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@githubnext` | `mise exec -- npm` falls back to **system** node v16.20.2, which writes to root-owned `/usr/lib`. |
| 3 | same for `Codex CLI` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@openai` | same |
| 4 | same for `Gemini CLI` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@google` (+ EBADENGINE warnings — needs node ≥20) | same |
| 5 | same for `OpenChamber` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@openchamber` | same |
| 6 | `rust_cargo_tools : Install Rust via mise` | `could not download nonexistent rust version 1.95.0 … 404` from `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup` | TUNA mirror has GC'd / not yet pulled rust 1.95.0; `~/.cargo/config.toml` redirects rustup there. |

**All six are solvable.** They share one upstream cause: [`dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl) (lines 8-19, 30-43) intentionally **omits `node` and `rust`** from mise's `[tools]` on CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17 baseline, TUNA mirror gap), but the ansible roles don't know that and blindly call `mise exec -- npm …` / `mise install rust@latest`.

The mise config-file comment block (lines 33-37) already documents the manual fallbacks:

- Node.js: NodeSource RPM (skipped here per user choice — EL7 ships node 16 only, too old for the agents anyway).
- Rust: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`.

This plan codifies those fallbacks in ansible so a fresh `chezmoi apply` on EL7 stops failing.

## User-confirmed decisions

- **Node-based CLIs on EL7** → **skip cleanly** (don't try system node 16 with `--prefix ~/.local`; node <20 breaks most of them at runtime anyway).
- **Rust on EL7** → **skip mise's rust install, run `rustup-init` directly** (the path the mise config comment already prescribes).

## Approach

Single shared `oldEL` fact + per-role guard, mirroring the `$oldEL` template logic in `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl:8-19`. No new pitfall surfaces — extend the existing `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md` notes and add a one-liner cross-link.

### Step 1 — Define `oldEL` once, in the playbook

File: [`dot_ansible/playbooks/site.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/site.yml) (or wherever the top-level `pre_tasks:` for Linux lives — verify during execution).

Add a `pre_tasks` (Linux-only) `set_fact` so every role can reference it:

\```yaml
- name: Detect CentOS/RHEL 7 (glibc 2.17 baseline) — mirrors mise config.toml.tmpl $oldEL
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    oldEL: >-
      {{ ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
         and (ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] | string) == '7' }}
  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
\```

(For non-RedHat hosts `oldEL` stays undefined and the `default(false)` filter in role `when:` clauses keeps it falsy.)

### Step 2 — Gate `rust_cargo_tools` on `oldEL` and add rustup-init fallback

File: [`dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml:18-23`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml).

Replace the single `Install Rust via mise` task with a two-branch pattern:

\```yaml
- name: Install Rust via mise (non-EL7)
  when: not (oldEL | default(false))
  ansible.builtin.command: "{{ mise_bin }} install rust@latest"
  args:
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/share/mise/installs/rust"
  environment:
    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"

# CentOS 7 / RHEL 7: mise's rustup channel goes through the TUNA mirror which
# garbage-collects old versions; rust@latest 404s when TUNA hasn't pulled the
# newest release yet. Use upstream rustup-init directly — it respects the
# user's ~/.cargo/config.toml mirror for crates.io but ignores TUNA for the
# toolchain download. Documented in dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl:36-37.
- name: Install Rust via rustup-init (CentOS/RHEL 7 fallback)
  when: oldEL | default(false)
  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    if [ -x "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin/cargo" ]; then
      echo "ALREADY_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs \
      | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable --no-modify-path
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin/cargo"
  environment:
    RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER: "https://static.rust-lang.org"
    RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT: "https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup"
\```

## Approved Plan:
# CentOS 7 (`idc-server104`) chezmoi-apply failures — fix plan

## Context

User `yczhang` ran `chezmoi update --apply --init` on a CentOS 7.9 box (`centos_server` profile, passwordless sudo) and hit five ansible task failures:

| # | Task | Error | Root cause |
|---|------|-------|------------|
| 1 | `lazyvim_deps : Install tree-sitter-cli via cargo (fallback)` | `Unable to find libclang … libclangAST.so.7 cannot open` | Cargo path triggered because the prior `mise exec -- npm install -g tree-sitter-cli` couldn't actually use mise's node (none managed on EL7); CentOS 7's `clang-devel` is split and the cargo+bindgen build fails to link libclang at runtime. |
| 2 | `coding_agents : Install GitHub Copilot CLI via mise npm` | `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@githubnext` | `mise exec -- npm` falls back to **system** node v16.20.2, which writes to root-owned `/usr/lib`. |
| 3 | same for `Codex CLI` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@openai` | same |
| 4 | same for `Gemini CLI` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@google` (+ EBADENGINE warnings — needs node ≥20) | same |
| 5 | same for `OpenChamber` | same `EACCES /usr/lib/node_modules/@openchamber` | same |
| 6 | `rust_cargo_tools : Install Rust via mise` | `could not download nonexistent rust version 1.95.0 … 404` from `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/rustup` | TUNA mirror has GC'd / not yet pulled rust 1.95.0; `~/.cargo/config.toml` redirects rustup there. |

**All six are solvable.** They share one upstream cause: [`dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl) (lines 8-19, 30-43) intentionally **omits `node` and `rust`** from mise's `[tools]` on CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17 baseline, TUNA mirror gap), but the ansible roles don't know that and blindly call `mise exec -- npm …` / `mise install rust@latest`.

The mise config-file comment block (lines 33-37) already documents the manual fallbacks:

- Node.js: NodeSource RPM (skipped here per user choice — EL7 ships node 16 only, too old for the agents anyway).
- Rust: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`.

This plan codifies those fallbacks in ansible so a fresh `chezmoi apply` on EL7 stops failing.

## User-confirmed decisions

- **Node-based CLIs on EL7** → **skip cleanly** (don't try system node 16 with `--prefix ~/.local`; node <20 breaks most of them at runtime anyway).
- **Rust on EL7** → **skip mise's rust install, run `rustup-init` directly** (the path the mise config comment already prescribes).

## Approach

Single shared `oldEL` fact + per-role guard, mirroring the `$oldEL` template logic in `dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl:8-19`. No new pitfall surfaces — extend the existing `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md` notes and add a one-liner cross-link.

### Step 1 — Define `oldEL` once, in the playbook

File: [`dot_ansible/playbooks/site.yml`](../../dot_ansible/playbooks/site.yml) (or wherever the top-level `pre_tasks:` for Linux lives — verify during execution).

Add a `pre_tasks` (Linux-only) `set_fact` so every role can reference it:

```yaml
- name: Detect CentOS/RHEL 7 (glibc 2.17 baseline) — mirrors mise config.toml.tmpl $oldEL
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    oldEL: >-
      {{ ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
         and (ansible_facts['distribution_major_version'] | string) == '7' }}
  when: ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
```

(For non-RedHat hosts `oldEL` stays undefined and the `default(false)` filter in role `when:` clauses keeps it falsy.)

### Step 2 — Gate `rust_cargo_tools` on `oldEL` and add rustup-init fallback

File: [`dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml:18-23`](../../dot_ansible/roles/rust_cargo_tools/tasks/main.yml).

Replace the single `Install Rust via mise` task with a two-branch pattern:

```yaml

  ansible.builtin.command: "{{ mise_bin }} install rust@latest"

  ansible.builtin.shell: |
    set -e
    if [ -x "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin/cargo" ]; then
      echo "ALREADY_INSTALLED"
      exit 0
    fi
    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs \
      | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain stable --no-modify-path
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash
    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.cargo/bin/cargo"
  environment:
    RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER: "https://static.rust-lang.org"
    RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT: "https://static.rust-lang.org/rustup"
```

Downstream `cargo install` tasks (lines 29-37, 46-50, etc.) already prepend `~/.cargo/bin` to PATH — they pick up the rustup-installed cargo without further changes.

 `./pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`

```text
126	
127	
128	The user-level fallbacks in `base/tasks/main.yml` already prefer
129	**musl** assets where upstream offers them — `ripgrep`, `fd`, `lnav`
130	all ship `*-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` variants that are statically
131	linked and ignore glibc version. Those are fine on CentOS 7.
132	
133	Tools that ship glibc-only binaries (some Go releases, some Rust
134	releases without musl variants) will fail. Workarounds, in order of
135	preference:
136	
137	1. **Cargo source build** — `cargo install <crate>` works on CentOS 7
138	   via the user's mise/cargo toolchain (`rust_cargo_tools` role
139	   already sets this up).
140	2. **Older release pin** — find a release built before the upstream
141	   project moved to a newer Ubuntu CI, pin to it.
142	3. **Skip on CentOS 7** — for tools that aren't critical, gate the
143	   block on `ansible_distribution_major_version != "7"` and live
144	   without it.
145	
146	If the box gets rebuilt as Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 (glibc 2.28 / 2.34), most
147	of these go away — the gate-broadening fix above is still correct on
148	those.
149	
150	## Required preconditions on a noRoot CentOS box
```
</details></tool-use>
